values.question: Where does the model err at the rule, and can its score be read as a probability?
values.segment_rule: The first two categorical features the model uses, in the order of the case; at most 12 values each, the rarer ones folded into "(other values)".

curve.definition: For the top share of the rows by score: recall is the share of the positive rows found (the cumulative gain, and the true positive rate of the ROC curve); lift is the precision over the base rate; the false positive rate is the share of the negative rows selected.

calibration.binning: 10 equal-count bins of the score, in score order
calibration.definition: The Brier score is the mean squared difference between the score and the outcome (0 or 1); the constant base rate gives the reference. A bin whose mean score lies outside the interval of its observed rate is miscalibrated.

segments.small_cell_rule: fewer than 30 rows or fewer than 10 selected rows
fewer than 30 rows or fewer than 10 selected rows

examples.note: Rows whose selection at the rule disagrees with the outcome, with the feature values as written in the file. Examples to read, not a sample.

point_check.note: The coefficients and their intervals come from the same prepared rows and the same penalised fit.

coefficients.method: Wald intervals, estimate +- z * standard error, from the sandwich covariance H^-1 B H^-1 of the fit on every prepared row (H the penalised information, B the spread of the row scores): the delta-method approximation of a nonparametric bootstrap
coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects. The fit is penalised: its coefficients are pulled towards zero, so the intervals describe the spread of the penalised estimate, centred on a value that is itself shrunk; they are not exact confidence intervals of an unpenalised coefficient, and a coefficient of a rare category can be shrunk well inside its interval.
coefficients.scale: per standard deviation of the training rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot); associations, not effects

values.note: Development evidence: computed on the validation predictions, on which the model and the rule were chosen. These figures describe the choice; they are not independent evidence.

calibration_slope.definition: slope of a logistic regression of the outcome on the logit of the score: 1 when the scores are as spread as the outcomes, below 1 when they are too extreme

linear_checks.method: binned out-of-fold gaps per numeric feature (chi-square, Bonferroni); calibration slope by segment (Cochran's Q); overall calibration slope (Cox 1958)
linear_checks.note: Checks of the candidate linear model on its out-of-fold predictions: a flag is evidence that another model family might follow the data more closely, not proof; choosing a family after seeing it makes that comparison data-contingent.
